transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, my sleep has been off. I'm usually very disciplined about it, but lately I just lie there. My cousin passed away recently, and I keep replaying that night. When I do sleep, I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. with... just pieces of hospital images in my head. Then I have to go into board meetings feeling like I've only slept in fragments. It's not ideal.
How long have you been experiencing these sleep issues and feelings of distress since your cousin passed away?
It's been about three weeks. Just... ever since the night my cousin died in that highway collision.
Do you find yourself having upsetting thoughts or memories about your cousin's death coming into your mind when you don't want them to?

Yes. Sometimes. It's... usually when I'm not expecting it. Like if a phone rings late at night, or... if I'm driving and see the glare of headlights. I just get this sudden, sharp picture of the hospital corridor. Or I hear the police officer's voice again. It just pushes in, and I have to... take a moment to steady myself.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of your cousin's death?
No, I don't think so. My schedule is quite demanding, so... I can't really afford to just stop doing things. I've mostly just kept to my normal routine.
Have you had any upsetting dreams or nightmares about your cousin's death or that night at the hospital?
No, I haven't really had any dreams like that. At least, nothing I remember when I wake up. I just don't sleep very well in general right now.
Have you been feeling angry, guilty, or intensely sad about what happened with your cousin?

No, not really. I mean... it's a tragic situation, of course. But I wouldn't say I've felt angry or... guilty. I just don't really dwell on those kinds of emotions. I prefer to just focus on what needs to be handled.
Have you found yourself being more on edge or easily startled since your cousin passed away?

I don't know about easily startled. But... I suppose I have been a bit more on edge, mostly just when I'm driving. 

I just find myself constantly checking the mirrors now, or watching the speed of the trucks around me... looking for where I could pull off if I needed to. Even just on the familiar roads taking my usual route to the office, my body stays tight. It's just... like I'm waiting for something to happen, I guess.
Have you noticed yourself feeling numb or detached from others or activities since your cousin passed away?

I suppose. Um... during the prayer gatherings, and when my nieces were trying to comfort me... I behaved properly, of course. But... I just didn't really feel any warmth or relief inside. It was almost as if... the affectionate part of me had just gone quiet. I just did what was expected of me.
Have you experienced any sleep disturbances or nightmares that feel connected to the night your cousin passed away, even if you don't remember specific dreams?

Well, yes. That's actually why I decided to come in. I'm usually quite disciplined about my sleep... it's necessary for my schedule. But lately, I just lie there. 

I end up replaying that night in my head. And when I do manage to drift off, I... I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. It's usually just... fragments of things. Images from the hospital, mostly. I don't really remember full dreams. But it leaves me going into my board meetings feeling like I've only slept in pieces.
Since your cousin passed away, have you noticed a lasting feeling of emptiness or an inability to feel happiness, even during moments that used to bring you joy?

No... I don't think so. I wouldn't say I feel empty. I mean, I'm still functioning perfectly well at the office, and... I can still appreciate a successful week or a quiet evening. I haven't noticed anything like that. It's really just the sleep that is the issue.
Have you had any recurrent dreams or nightmares since your cousin passed away that have left you feeling upset, even if you don't remember the exact content?

I think I already mentioned that. Like I said, I don't really remember full dreams... just fragments of the hospital. I wake up, and it's difficult to get back to sleep. But I wouldn't call them recurrent nightmares. It's just... disruptive.
Have you had any dreams or nightmares since your cousin passed away that left you feeling upset, even if you can't remember the exact details?
Doctor, I believe you just asked me that. As I said... I don't really remember specific dreams. Just the fragments I mentioned before. It's disruptive, yes, but... that's all there is to it.
Has the disruption in your sleep caused you significant distress or affected your ability to function during the day, beyond just feeling tired?

Well... I suppose it's having some effect. I'm still making it to the essential meetings, of course. But... I've had to hand off some of my community obligations lately. And I've been cutting my workdays a bit shorter. I'm just... not quite as steady, or as effective with people as I usually am right now.
Has the broken sleep been causing you distress or making it hard to do things you normally would, even outside of work or obligations?
I... I think we just covered that. I already mentioned I've been stepping back from some of my community things. I don't really have anything else to add to that. It's just what I said.

Since your cousin passed away, have you noticed any negative changes in your thoughts or mood, such as feeling overly negative about yourself or the world, or losing interest in activities you used to care about?

I suppose... well, things have felt a bit muted. At the prayer gatherings, and when my nieces were trying to be comforting... I did what was expected. I behaved properly. But... I didn't really feel any warmth from it. No relief. It's just... quiet, in that regard. Like that part of me is just... not there right now.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more depressed, irritable, or emotionally drained lately, even outside of the times when you're reminded of your cousin?

I suppose... yes, I've been a bit more irritable. I... well, I snapped at my leadership team recently. Over very minor things. Small delays, the wording in some emails. I used a tone that I would normally consider entirely unacceptable. It's... embarrassing, honestly. They haven't really done anything wrong, but my patience is just... very thin right now.
Have you been experiencing intrusive thoughts or memories about the night your cousin passed away that cause you significant distress or make it hard for you to function in your daily life?

I suppose... yes. Just at odd moments. If I hear a phone ring late, or... see the glare of headlights on the highway. I'll get this very sharp picture of the hospital corridor, or... I'll hear the police officer’s voice again. It just pushes into my mind. I usually just have to pause for a moment to steady myself. But... yes, it happens.
